reader.requirement: At 85 a space may optionally precede every separator (comma, semicolon, period, parentheses, colon, opening quotation mark, closing pseudo-text delimiter) without changing the program's meaning, except where reference format rules govern (continuation), before a closing quotation mark (where the space is part of the nonnumeric literal), and before an opening pseudo-text delimiter (where the space is required).
reader.edition-search: grep Edition|Version|Year|dialect in SeparatorRule.cs (its summary states it is edition-invariant; only the Editions namespace import), PictureSeparatorPeriodRule.cs (none), CobolLexer.g4 WS/DOT/FNARG_SEPARATOR/LPAREN/RPAREN/PIC_STRING rules (the lexer's only edition read is _caseMappingEdition, word case folding, not separators) and CopyProcessor.cs#ReadOperand (none).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f03_01 and 1985-SR-IV_4_2_1-8 cover a space before comma, semicolon, period, parentheses and the closing quotation mark; not exercised there: a space before the colon of a reference modifier, before a closing pseudo-text delimiter, before the period of headers and data entries, before the separator after a PICTURE string, and the reference-format exception (a continued literal and a continued word)

probes.expected: spaces before every separator are inert: W-STR ( 2 : 3 ), REPLACE == XX1 == BY == W-A == ., PIC X(3) , VALUE, PIC 9(3) ; VALUE, T ( I ), FUNCTION LENGTH ( W-STR ), IF ( ... ), headers ending ' .'; a space before the closing quote is literal content; a continued literal keeps the spaces up to margin R and a continued word DIS/-PLAY joins (reference format exception a)

probes.printed: error COBOL2573: REPLACE statement: the opening == follows 'E' with no space
probes.expected: exception c: the space before an opening pseudo-text delimiter is required

citations.check: OK  §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR8  (4.2.1 Separators)  the text is in SR8

reader.notes: The lexer skips WS and the comma/semicolon-plus-space separator outside list regions, so a preceding space never changes a token; literals keep their spaces; ReadOperand enforces exception c. No edition is consulted on this path. A first sr8 run (sr8-001) differed only because the probe's own line overran column 72; the corrected probe matched.

refuter.evidence: s89.cob at --std 85 (runs s89-002): a space before every period of headers, entries and sentences (PROGRAM-ID . S89SUB ., END PROGRAM S89 .), before commas and semicolons in a two-subscript reference TC ( 2 , 3 ), in an 88 VALUE 1 , 3 ; 5 ., in CALL USING W , K and PROCEDURE DIVISION USING LW , LK, in FUNCTION MAX ( 3 , 9 ; 4 ), before ':' and ')' in W ( 2 : 3 ) and W( K :1 ): every separator line printed as expected (74 / BCDDEA / 09 / ODD / XYZDEF). The one differing line is the DISPLAY of N PIC S9V9 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE (printed -0.5 for a 3-character item), a DISPLAY conversion question (§1985:VI.6.10.4 GR1, implementor-defined), not a separator. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR8  (4.2.1 Separators)  the text is in SR8'.
